newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Saudi's Savola Q1 net profit rises, announces dividend.
newsitem.headline: Saudi's Savola Q1 net profit rises, announces dividend.

text.p: Savola Company of Saudi Arabia said its net profit for the first three months of 1997 increased 3.6 million riyals to 28.7 million riyals.
This represents a 14 percent rise over first quarter 1996.
A company statement said the board had decided to pay a 25 riyal per share dividend for 1996, when it posted net profits of over 140 million riyals.
The statement showed shareholders' funds rising 5.7 percent in the first quarter to 1.015 billion riyals.
Savola said its $119 million sugar refinery in Jeddah would start commercial production in the first half of this year.
Savola, which owns 51 percent of the United Sugar Co refinery, built it with Tate and Lyle Plc, which holds 15 percent, and 13 Saudi sugar traders.
Traded on the Saudi stock market, the firm is the country's biggest food group.
